extracted.intended_audience: persons submitting claims under Article 139 (UCMJ), military commanders and legal staff, and agricultural stakeholders (growers, handlers, committees) affected by USDA marketing orders
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedures for processing claims under Article 139 of the Uniform Code of Military Justice (property damage/wrongful taking by Army personnel), together with related notice-and-comment and marketing-order procedural requirements for agricultural stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope — applicability of section
rubrics_metrics.description: This section applies to claims for damage to, or loss or destruction of, property owned or in the lawful possession of an individual, a business, a charity, a State or local government, or a service member, that has been willfully damaged or destroyed or wrongfully taken by military personnel of the Army.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies who may bring claims (owners or lawful possessors including businesses, charities, governmental entities, and service members) and the types of property incidents covered (willful damage, destruction, wrongful taking by Army personnel).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — willful damage
rubrics_metrics.description: Willful damage: Damage which is inflicted intentionally, knowingly, and purposely, without justifiable excuse, as distinguished from damage which is caused thoughtlessly or inadvertently as in simple negligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes willful (intentional) conduct from simple negligence (inadvertent), which affects compensability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — wrongful taking
rubrics_metrics.description: Wrongful taking: Any unauthorized taking or withholding of property, not involving breach of contractual or fiduciary relationships, with intent to deprive the owner or person in lawful possession of his property temporarily, permanently, or for an indefinite period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers larceny-like acts; excludes contractual/fiduciary breaches; requires intent to deprive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — board of officers
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'board of officers' includes an investigating officer appointed under the provisions of §§ 519.1-519.5 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines which investigative bodies qualify as 'board of officers' for purposes of recommendation and processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims payable — willful damage/riotous or depredation acts
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims for damage to or loss or destruction of property caused by riotous, violent, and disorderly conduct, or acts of depredation, by a member or members of the Army, or acts showing such reckless and wanton disregard of property rights that willful damage or destruction may reasonably be implied, are compensable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compensable when conduct is sufficiently violent/reckless to imply willfulness; factual determination required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims payable — wrongful taking (criminal-type losses)
rubrics_metrics.description: A loss through larceny, forgery, embezzlement, fraud, misappropriation, and similar offenses is compensable if a wrongful taking of property is involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates common wrongful-taking offenses that support a compensable claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims payable — acts outside scope of employment (with authority)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims for damage/loss/destruction that result from an act or omission that occurred outside the scope of a member’s employment which are cognizable under specified sections may be processed under this section, in whole or in part, if specific authority has been obtained from the responsible claims supervisory authority (§ 536.4a) or the Chief, U.S. Army Claims Service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires prior authorization from claims supervisory authority or Chief, U.S. Army Claims Service to process such out-of-scope incidents under this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims not payable — payable under other regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims that are payable under other regulations are not compensable under this section, except as provided in paragraph (e)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directs claimants to the proper regulatory channel where other regulations govern the loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims not payable — simple negligence excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims resulting from simple negligence are not compensable under this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple negligence (inadvertent, thoughtless damage) does not meet the willfulness standard required for compensation here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims not payable — subrogee claims excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims submitted by subrogees are not compensable under this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only original owners or lawful possessors may recover; insurers/subrogees cannot recover under this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims not payable — personal injury or death excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims for personal injury or death are not compensable under this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section is limited to property, not bodily injury or fatality claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims not payable — insured losses excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: Any portion of a claim covered by insurance, regardless of whether claim is made against the insurer, is not compensable under this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insurance coverage for the loss precludes payment under these Army claim provisions for that portion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims not payable — acts within scope of employment excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims resulting from acts or omissions of military personnel while acting within the scope of their employment are not compensable under this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Losses occurring within the scope of military employment are handled under other provisions (e.g., tort claims), not Article 139 processing here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims not payable — claimant-contributed negligence excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims for damages or losses in which the negligence or fault of the claimant, his employee or his agent contributed to the damage or loss are not compensable under this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributory negligence by claimant or agent bars recovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limitation for filing complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: In order for a claim to be considered under this section, a complaint must be submitted within 60 days of the date of the incident out of which the claim arose, unless the commander acting on the report determines that good cause has been shown for the delay in making complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sixty-day filing deadline is strict; commander’s finding that good cause was not shown is final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on amount of assessment against pay
rubrics_metrics.description: No assessment in excess of $250 will be made against the pay of any one offender for a single act or incident, without approval of The Judge Advocate General or his designee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caps financial assessments from offenders’ pay absent higher-level approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only direct damages considered
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment will be made only for direct damages. Indirect, remote, or inconsequential damages will not be considered under this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compensation limited to direct, proximate property damages; excludes consequential or remote losses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure — how to complain and claim form requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who believes his property has been willfully damaged or wrongfully taken may complain orally or in writing to the military organization or unit of the offending member(s) or the nearest Army installation. The complaint may be accompanied by a claim for damages. Such claim should be in writing, in triplicate, signed by the claimant or his authorized representative, and asserted in an amount certain. The claim may be regarded as the complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies locations to file complaints, recommended claim format (written, triplicate, signed, amount certain), and that a claim can serve as the complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary restitution — effect on official claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Members who cause damage through off-duty activities may make restitution without the matter becoming official; acceptance by the complainant of payment in full bars further recovery under this section. Any amount paid in partial satisfaction will be deducted from the amount approved by the commanding officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages voluntary settlements; full settlement precludes later official recovery; partial payments reduce official award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions of payment — required preconditions prior to payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to payment of any claim within this section, conditions that must be fulfilled include: the claim is in writing and for a definite amount; the complaint was presented within 60 days or good cause shown; the damage was not covered by insurance; the amount has been determined; the claim relates to property other than Government property; the claim did not result from simple negligence; the property was willfully damaged/destroyed or wrongfully taken by Army member(s); the claim was not presented by a subrogee; claimant's negligence did not contribute; payment was recommended by the board of officers and approved personally by the offender’s commanding officer; the staff judge advocate determined proceedings were legally sufficient; the commanding officer ordered a stoppage of pay; and the assessment against each offender does not exceed $250 except as approved by The Judge Advocate General.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive checklist of prerequisites to payment (many items echo earlier standalone provisions); payment requires procedural and substantive approvals and administrative actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission requirements — cotton spot markets proposed amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed amendments to § 27.93 and § 27.94: interested persons wishing to submit written views or arguments must file them in duplicate with the Hearing Clerk, U.S. Department of Agriculture, Washington, D.C., not later than 30 days after publication of the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions will be made available for public inspection during regular business hours per 7 CFR 1.27; gives copy-number (duplicate) and 30-day deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission requirements — navel oranges assessment proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons desiring to submit written data, views, or arguments regarding proposed expenses and rate of assessment should file them in quadruplicate with the Hearing Clerk, U.S. Department of Agriculture, Room 112, Administration Building, Washington, D.C., not later than the 10th day after publication in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies quadruplicate copies and 10-day deadline; submissions will be made available for public inspection at the Hearing Clerk's office (7 CFR 1.27(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of public hearing — cranberry marketing amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice is given of public hearings to receive evidence with respect to the economic and marketing conditions related to proposed amendments; hearings are scheduled at specified dates, times, and locations in multiple states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to take evidence on economic/marketing conditions; proposed amendments have not yet received Secretary approval; attendees may present evidence relevant to the amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — fiscal period (cranberry order)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Fiscal period' is synonymous with 'fiscal year' and 'crop year' and means the 12-month period beginning September 1 of one year and ending August 31 of the following year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies temporal unit for administration and reporting under the order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — base quantity (cranberry order)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Base quantity' means the number of pounds of cranberries established for a grower by the committee pursuant to § 929.48.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base quantity is the foundational unit used for allotments; see § 929.48 for computation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — marketable quantity (cranberry order)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Marketable quantity' means for a crop year the number of pounds of cranberries necessary to meet the total market demand and to provide for an adequate carryover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to determine allotments and regulate supply to meet demand and carryover needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — annual allotment (cranberry order)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Annual allotment' means for a grower in a particular crop year a quantity equivalent to the number of pounds of cranberries determined by multiplying the base quantity of such grower by the allotment percentage established pursuant to § 929.49 for such crop year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual allotment = base quantity × allotment percentage; governs how much each grower may market/handle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — established cranberry acreage
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Established cranberry acreage' means acreage which is presently producing cranberries on a commercial basis or acreage which has been recently planted or will be planted prior to August 1, 1968, to produce cranberries on a commercial basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affects eligibility for base quantity computations and related determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marketing policy content requirements (committee report)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each crop year prior to making certain recommendations the committee shall submit to the Secretary a report setting forth its marketing policy for the crop year and the basis therefor, including information relating to: estimated total production; expected general quality of production; estimated carryover (as of Sept 1) of frozen cranberries and other cranberry products; expected demand conditions in different market outlets; supplies of competing commodities; trend and level of consumer income; the recommended desirable total marketable quantity including recommended adequate carryover into the following crop year; regulation pursuant to § 929.52 expected recommendations; and other factors bearing on marketing of cranberries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the data/factors the committee must analyze and report to justify marketing recommendations (supply, demand, quality, carryover, competition, income trends, and other relevant factors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary regulation — handler recording of grower identity and quantity
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning with the 1968-69 crop year, no handler shall handle, as the first handler, cranberries purchased from a grower or acquired for handling for a grower until the handler has determined the identity of the grower and the quantity of cranberries attributed to such grower. The handler shall furnish such information to the committee at such times and in such forms as the committee, with the approval of the Secretary, may request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires handlers to track and report grower identity and quantities to enable base quantity establishment and allotment administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee duty — furnish producer reporting form
rubrics_metrics.description: So that each producer may qualify for a base quantity pursuant to § 929.48, the committee shall furnish each producer early in each calendar year a form to be filed with the committee whereon the producer reports the location of his bog(s), the acreage he intends to harvest for cranberries, and such other information as the committee needs to establish a base quantity for such producer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee must proactively provide forms and collect requisite producer information to establish base quantities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base quantity determination rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon the Secretary finding that the six crop years 1968-69 through 1973-74 constitute a representative period, a base quantity shall be computed for each qualified grower (generally as established acreage × average per acre sales during the two crop years with greatest sales within that period). The committee shall establish each grower’s base quantity based on handler reports, grower certifications, and other information. Provisions are included for relocation of acreage lost due to unusual circumstances and for committee/Secretary rules to implement the section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed computational method and special-case rules (relocation, new control of acreage) to determine each grower’s base quantity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional base quantities — when demand exceeds aggregate base
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting in 1974-75, if market demand exceeds aggregate base quantities, the committee shall consider and, if appropriate with Secretary approval, grant additional base quantities to new or existing growers to satisfy increased market demand, insofar as practicable by increasing all existing base quantities and establishing base quantities for new growers due to new acreage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows adjustment of base quantities to respond to increased market demand, subject to committee consideration and Secretary approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marketable quantity and allotment percentage — determination and apportionment
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning with the 1974-75 crop year, the Secretary may determine and establish the marketable quantity for the crop year (if limiting quantity would effectuate the declared policy). The marketable quantity shall be apportioned among growers by applying an allotment percentage to each grower’s base quantity. The allotment percentage equals marketable quantity divided by total of all growers’ base quantities. Except as provided, no handler shall purchase or handle cranberries from a grower beyond that grower’s annual allotment. Committee/Secretary may increase or suspend allotment percentage when appropriate; committee may recommend increasing marketable quantity if demand proves greater than set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the formula for apportionment (allotment percentage) and governs restrictions on handling/purchases relative to annual allotments; includes modification mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuance of annual allotments — grower filing and committee issuance dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Each grower must qualify for his allotment by filing with the committee on or before February 1 a CMC form stating where he intends to produce his annual allotment, acreage to be harvested, location changes, and other necessary information. On or before May 1 the committee shall issue to each grower an annual allotment determined by applying the allotment percentage to the grower’s base quantity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies calendar deadlines for grower qualification (Feb 1) and for committee to issue allotments (May 1) each year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filling deficiencies in annual allotments — permitted mechanisms and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: If a grower does not produce cranberries equal to his computed annual allotment, he may (1) fill the deficit by obtaining cranberries from another grower who has excess; (2) transfer any unused portion of his allotment to another grower; or (3) transfer his unused allotment to a handler who shall allocate it to other growers with insufficient allotment. As a condition to any such transfer each grower or handler shall furnish a full report to the committee including names of parties, quantity involved, and other information to enable administration. The committee with Secretary approval may modify these provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides flexibility for reallocating allotments to meet demand while requiring reporting for administrative tracking and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee clearing-house service
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee shall act as a clearing house of information on producers with deficits in production and the availability of cranberries in excess of salable; such information shall be available at the committee office to any producer or handler upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee provides a matching/information service to facilitate transfers and meeting market demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfers of base quantity — location transfers and transfers to other growers
rubrics_metrics.description: A grower may transfer the base quantity from the acreage to which it was attributed to other land he owns or leases, subject to committee approval and (if transferor is not owner) owner's consent; a grower may transfer all or part of a base quantity to another grower, but transfers are recognized only upon written notice to the committee and transferee evidence of capability to produce and harvest the base quantity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfers require committee notification/approval and owner consent where applicable; transferee must demonstrate production capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination — periodic referenda of growers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary shall conduct a referendum during May 1975 to ascertain whether continuance of the part is favored by growers, and shall conduct such a referendum during the month of May of every fourth year thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes periodic democratic review by affected growers on whether the marketing order should continue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class I price differential criteria (Tri-State milk marketing decision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination of Class I differentials should consider the basic formula price plus a fixed differential, supply-demand adjustments, historical weighted-average differentials, competitive alignment with neighboring Federal order markets, overlapping sales/distribution areas, effects on handlers' competitiveness for sales contracts, and evidence presented by cooperatives/handlers/producers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates evidence and policy considerations used to set district differentials (e.g., weighted averages of past differentials, supply-demand adjustments, price alignment to reduce competitive disadvantages among districts or with nearby markets).
